description: Hero case for false safety. On Debian 13, php8.4-fpm was put on hold with apt-mark hold, a common way to avoid surprise FPM restarts, so the last apt upgrade patched php8.4-cli and php8.4-common to 8.4.27-1~deb13u1 and skipped FPM, which dpkg shows as held (hi) at 8.4.16-1~deb13u1. php -v reports the patched CLI, so anything reading php -v clears the host, while the FPM package that serves traffic is affected. The verdict must be per package, and php -v must not be treated as evidence about php8.4-fpm.
stack: Debian 13 trixie, nginx with php8.4-fpm, php8.4-fpm held with apt-mark hold
why: OSV: Debian:13 php8.4 fixed in 8.4.27-1~deb13u1. php8.4-cli 8.4.27-1~deb13u1 is fixed, php8.4-fpm 8.4.16-1~deb13u1 is affected.
